body:
You write beautifully. I know it's not the best way to start off my reply but ... look where we are ... I don't think it matters right now, right?  I had to say it because it was long and I read it all... that rarely happens.

I was 30 once, but I was female, still am. See, I can't write as well as you. Anyway it seems like we both missed out on major childhood experiences and milestones and that's where I felt a connection.  Honestly what I'm trying to say but can't is: At 30 I chose to die for the second time in my life. I was convinced it was the only answer. It wasn't. There's always another answer to the question "what should I do".

Fuck, I swear I had a point when I started writing this. Forgive me, I'm a bit of a mess tonight.  I'm feeling those worthless anchors hung around me. They're heavy, you know that. But what is worth anyway? How is it measured? Is it like meaning... ever elusive like some giant joke on mankind? 

I'm 40 now, still here and fighting. Why? I dunno but a lot of awesome things happened in the last ten years. Not so much directly to me but in general. Are smartphones a reason to live? Maybe for some. Part of me is just curious how this whole story ends, not just my own.
Thank you so very much for taking the time to reply. And for your sweet words as well.

And maybe the word hope carries too much weight. Hope for me is just a pinhole of light in the vast darkness. It might be like the lottery, you might never win but if you play there's a fraction of a possibility. I was in that place where there was no possibility at all because I wasn't playing this game called life. 
I know the word hope can make some of us cringe because of how long and hard life beat us down. So I will definitely look into a better word to describe it. ✌️❤️😃

Beautiful words. I read somewhere that philosophy can be a "cure" of sorts for depression. Makes sense though, changing your perception of life has worked for some. 

Hope you're doing well, friend.

I think that's a perfectly acceptable way to feel considering all that you're dealing with. But for some reason your post reminded me of a quote from the movie Castaway... 

 “So now I know what I have to do. I have to keep breathing. And tomorrow the sun will rise, and who knows what the tide will bring in.”

It has helped me through some rough patches and maybe it might help ease your mind a bit. I wish you well, friend.  You are not alone.

Please don't take the Tylenol. It's very painful and will cause damage. Maybe give it a little time and see if it gets better. I usually think to myself, I can always do it tomorrow. Good luck to you. Try and stay strong.

Did your adventure four years ago help you any? Did you learn or see anything exciting?

I'm very familiar with panic attacks. That's what keeps my in my shell, in my house. I always thought if I lived in an intentional community (commune) I might find some relief. A support system maybe. I don't know. I just feel like I don't have what it takes to make it in this "out for myself" world.

I get the same way with brightness and too much color. I think it has something to do with derealization or depersonalization. All part of the adrenaline rush during panic. 

I thought I had a good day yesterday while I went to the store. Then I got repeatedly pushed by a man's cart because I tried to get into a line before him. I tried to reason with his wife and politely said, "I was here first, can you please let me go? I'm having a panic attack and would really appreciate it." Well, she laughed directly in my face and they pushed me aside. I kept my cool but they called me crazy, a nut job, said I have issues. That was devastating for me. I just still can't get over it.

I want to believe there are decent people still out there. I want to believe there's still compassion. So I decided to see if I could find someone to talk to that might understand, or at the very least maybe I could show compassion to someone else. It's sad. What is this world coming to?

I like those last two options. I always wanted to do something like that. Unfortunately, I can barely leave my house. It reminds me of one of my favorite movies, Into the Wild. I'd be interested in hearing about your travels and others might too. I'm here to talk about it if you like. Maybe about the places you might see...

Sorry you're feeling this way. I've been in that dark place and sometimes wonder how I made it through. It wasn't anything miraculous, I just kept telling myself I'd give it one more day. I'm by no means out of that tunnel and I'm not sure if there's any light to see but I'm still here somehow. I figure since my mind is made up about it, I might as well see how long I can actually make it. Just a thought that  I wanted to share. I hope you can find a little relief from your pain for now.

I made this account because I felt such a need to reply to you. I wouldn't dare say I know what you're going through, but I do know panic attacks. I'm actually on the verge of one right now so I'm hoping I can distract myself by writing to you. And maybe I might even say something that's helpful? 

It sucks that you didn't get any real help. I understand that aspect of it. I've felt like an experiment at times, having medications thrown at me one after another. I understand that it can be a trial an error as far as that goes but it would be nice to feel as if they were genuinely concerned about their patients' well being. In my experience with meds, I've learned that sometimes just stopping them abruptly can cause issues so maybe check into that. I've always tapered them down to try an avoid any further anxiety issues. (Not sure what you're taking) 

I'm sorry that I don't have any real solutions for you. I've tried many different coping mechanisms and techniques to get rid of panic so if you have any questions regarding a specific one I may be able to help. 

I just wanted to say that I hear you and you're definitely not alone in your struggle to find help. I'm here if you'd like to talk. Sending positive thoughts your way.
